description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/lib.rs:71-90

```rust
/// Register all RFC 9670 JMAP Sharing method handlers with `dispatcher`.
///
/// `backend` is wrapped in [`Arc`] so it is cloned cheaply into each
/// handler. Pass the same `Arc<B>` to both this function and any
/// application-level code that needs to access the backend.
///
/// After this call, the dispatcher handles:
/// `Principal/get`, `Principal/changes`, `Principal/set`,
/// `Principal/query`, `Principal/queryChanges`,
/// `ShareNotification/get`, `ShareNotification/changes`,
/// `ShareNotification/set`, `ShareNotification/query`,
/// `ShareNotification/queryChanges`.
///
/// The dispatcher's `CallerCtx` is taken from `B::CallerCtx`; every
/// registered closure forwards it as `&ctx` into the wrapped `handle_*`
/// function. Backends that use `type CallerCtx = ()` therefore see
/// `&()` inside every handler.
pub fn register_sharing_handlers<B>(dispatcher: &mut Dispatcher<B::CallerCtx>, backend: Arc<B>)
where
    B: SharingBackend + 'static,
```

The doc covers what gets registered but not:

1. **Re-registration on conflict.** If `dispatcher` already has a
   handler for `Principal/get`, what happens? The behavior is
   inherited from `jmap_server::Dispatcher::register` (likely a
   silent HashMap overwrite, but the doc doesn't say). A caller who
   wants to wire \"my custom Principal/get plus the default
   everything else\" cannot tell whether they should register their
   custom one before or after this call.

2. **Idempotency.** Is calling `register_sharing_handlers` twice on
   the same dispatcher safe? With two different `Arc<B>` values? The
   doc doesn't say. If silent overwrite, the second call wins; if
   panic-on-conflict, both calls are unsafe in sequence.

3. **Capability advertisement.** The doc says \"After this call, the
   dispatcher handles ...\" — but the dispatcher is just method-name
   dispatch, not a JMAP Session capability advertiser. A caller who
   reads this and assumes the JMAP Session response automatically
   includes `urn:ietf:params:jmap:principals` will be wrong (per the
   workspace's consumer-brings-everything posture documented in the
   workspace AGENTS.md).

4. **Ordering relative to capability check.** The handlers do not
   inspect the `using` field — that validation is the
   dispatcher/framework layer's responsibility. The canonical
   mail-server's `register_mdn_handlers` (lib.rs:265-273) explicitly
   spells this out (\"Callers MUST ensure `check_known_capabilities`
   is called ...\"). Sharing-server has the same constraint but the
   doc is silent.

What goes wrong for callers when this stays as-is: a consumer
wires `register_sharing_handlers` without also wiring capability
validation, ships a deployment that accepts JMAP requests omitting
`urn:ietf:params:jmap:principals` in the `using` array, and serves
those requests as if the capability were present. RFC 8620 §3.3 is
violated silently.

Resolution: add a \"caller MUST also\" paragraph following the
`register_mdn_handlers` precedent. Document overwrite vs error on
re-registration (depends on upstream `Dispatcher::register`
contract).
notes: Expanded register_sharing_handlers rustdoc with (a) re-registration semantics (silent overwrite per Dispatcher::register HashMap shape, with override / try_register / double-call guidance), and (b) explicit note that this function does NOT advertise urn:ietf:params:jmap:principals in any Session capability response — that's the consumer's responsibility per workspace 'consumer-brings-everything' posture.
title: register_sharing_handlers — re-registration semantics undocumented; silent overwrite on conflict
